title: httpContext.Response.OnStarting lambdas executing in reverse order
author: mtamrakar

comments.body: @anurse I'm not sure `hosting` is the right area for this. Can you please adjust as necessary? Thanks!

This is intentional to mirror the middleware pipeline ordering. E.g. The last thing to register is the inner most component in the pipeline and so it gets to look at the response first.

Should update the doc comments to reflect this.

That said, what specific guidance did you get for using OnStarting? It's one of the harder APIs to use correctly, especially with complex interactions like this. You might do better to abstract the cookie handling to centralized logic and restrict to a single OnStarting event to apply the aggregate result.
Your second example is fine if you check HttpContext.Response.HasStarted first. No cookies can be modified after HasStarted, even with OnStarting.
Ideally, when would we ever do the OnStarting registration then?
OnStarting is useful for last second sanity checks, not much else.

Thank you. I'm closing the issue as OnStarting is doing what it supposed to and I do see that a comment update is in progress to clarify it's execution order.

I think we will just go with direct updates and handle out of sequence header updates more carefully.

satisfaction_conditions: Confirmation of the expected behavior of HttpContext.Response.OnStarting
Guidance on best practices for cookie management in ASP.NET Core
Clarification on appropriate use cases for OnStarting
Understanding of how to handle response headers that might be modified from different parts of the code

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

--- ./README.md ---
ASP.NET Core
============

ASP.NET Core is an open-source and cross-platform framework for building modern cloud based internet connected applications, such as web apps, IoT apps and mobile backends. ASP.NET Core apps can run on .NET Core or on the full .NET Framework. It was architected to provide an optimized development framework for apps that are deployed to the cloud or run on-premises. It consists of modular components with minimal overhead, so you retain flexibility while constructing your solutions. You can develop and run your ASP.NET Core apps cross-platform on Windows, Mac and Linux. [Learn more about ASP.NET Core](https://docs.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/).

--- ./src/Servers/Kestrel/test/SystemdActivation/Dockerfile ---
FROM microsoft/dotnet-nightly:2.0-runtime-deps

# The "container" environment variable is read by systemd.
ENV container=docker

# Install and configure dependencies.
RUN ["apt-get", "-o", "Acquire::Check-Valid-Until=false", "update"]
RUN ["apt-get", "install", "-y", "--no-install-recommends", "systemd", "socat"]

# Copy .NET installation.
ADD .dotnet/ /usr/share/dotnet/
RUN ["ln", "-s", "/usr/share/dotnet/dotnet", "/usr/bin/dotnet"]

# Copy "publish" app.
ADD publish/ /publish/

# Expose target ports.
EXPOSE 8080 8081 8082 8083 8084 8085

# Set entrypoint.
COPY ./docker-entrypoint.sh /
RUN chmod +x /docker-entrypoint.sh
ENTRYPOINT ["/docker-entrypoint.sh"]



--- ./src/Servers/Kestrel/samples/Http2SampleApp/Dockerfile ---
FROM microsoft/aspnetcore:2.0.0-stretch

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    libssl-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ARG CONFIGURATION=Debug

WORKDIR /app

COPY ./bin/${CONFIGURATION}/netcoreapp2.2/publish/ /app

ENTRYPOINT [ "/usr/bin/dotnet", "/app/Http2SampleApp.dll" ]

dockerfile:
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:3.1

WORKDIR /app

# Install git and other dependencies
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y git curl build-essential && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a test project to validate the OnStarting order issue
RUN dotnet new web -o OnStartingOrderTest

# Add a controller to demonstrate the issue
WORKDIR /app/OnStartingOrderTest
RUN mkdir -p Controllers && \
    echo 'using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; \
using System; \
using System.Threading.Tasks; \
\
namespace OnStartingOrderTest.Controllers \
{ \
    [ApiController] \
    [Route("/")] \
    public class HomeController : ControllerBase \
    { \
        [HttpGet] \
        public IActionResult Index() \
        { \
            HttpContext.Response.OnStarting( \
                () => \
                { \
                    Console.WriteLine(1); \
                    return Task.CompletedTask; \
                }); \
\
            HttpContext.Response.OnStarting( \
               () => \
               { \
                   Console.WriteLine(2); \
                   return Task.CompletedTask; \
               }); \
\
            HttpContext.Response.OnStarting( \
               () => \
               { \
                   Console.WriteLine(3); \
                   return Task.CompletedTask; \
               }); \
\
            HttpContext.Response.OnStarting( \
               () => \
               { \
                   Console.WriteLine(4); \
                   return Task.CompletedTask; \
               }); \
\
            HttpContext.Response.OnStarting( \
               () => \
               { \
                   Console.WriteLine(5); \
                   return Task.CompletedTask; \
               }); \
\
            HttpContext.Response.OnStarting( \
               () => \
               { \
                   Console.WriteLine(6); \
                   return Task.CompletedTask; \
               }); \
\
            HttpContext.Response.OnStarting( \
               () => \
               { \
                   Console.WriteLine(7); \
                   return Task.CompletedTask; \
               }); \
\
            return Ok("Check console output for OnStarting order"); \
        } \
    } \
}' > Controllers/HomeController.cs

# Build the test project
RUN dotnet build

# Clone the repository at a specific commit (with a shallow clone to save space)
WORKDIR /app
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore.git && \
    cd aspnetcore && \
    git fetch --depth=1 origin 085f6e158520b3ddc2e7ed7398bc970a442d4520 && \
    git checkout FETCH_HEAD

# Set the entry point to bash so the container stays running
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash"]
